messages.content: Give me an analysis trail for my project SUPERFANCY with component UUID AB1010CD and vulnerability ef903ac-893-f00

function.name: acl_api_AclApi_retrieve_projects
function.description: Retrieve a list of projects assigned to the specified team, with options to exclude inactive projects and/or omit child projects. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

uuid.description: The unique identifier of the team for which projects are being retrieved.

excludeInactive.description: If set to true, inactive projects will not be included in the response.

onlyRoot.description: If set to true, only root projects will be returned, excluding their child projects.

function.name: analysis_api_AnalysisApi_retrieve_analysis
function.description: Retrieves the detailed analysis trail for a given project, component, and vulnerability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

project.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the project for which the analysis trail is retrieved.

component.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the component associated with the project.

vulnerability.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the vulnerability within the component.

message.content: I’m not sure I have the correct identifiers to retrieve the analysis trail. Could you please provide the UUID of the project “SUPERFANCY” (or confirm that “SUPERFANCY” is the UUID itself)? Once I have the proper UUID, I can fetch the analysis trail for component AB1010CD and vulnerability ef903ac-893-f00.
message.reasoning: The user wants an analysis trail for a project named SUPERFANCY with component UUID AB1010CD and vulnerability ef903ac-893-f00. We need to call the analysis_api_AnalysisApi_retrieve_analysis function. The function expects project, component, vulnerability as strings. The project is "SUPERFANCY" but the function expects a UUID. The user gave a name, not a UUID. We might need to retrieve the project UUID first. But we don't have a function to get project by name. We only have retrieve_projects which returns projects for a team. We don't have a team ID. So we cannot retrieve the project by name. The user might have provided the project name incorrectly. We could ask for clarification. But the instruction says: "If you do not have enough information to answer the question, ask for clarification." So we should ask for clarification: what is the UUID of the project? Or maybe we can assume the project name is the UUID? But that seems wrong. The function expects a UUID. So we need clarification.
